description:
## Finding
\`pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:154-166\` \`cert_is_ca\` uses \`.ok()\` on \`BasicConstraints::from_der\`, treating malformed BC as not-CA. The doc comment explicitly justifies this as \"fail-open for the builder\" because validate_path will catch structural problems later.

## Why P2
- The doc justification is partially correct (pkix-path's per-cert structural checks would reject a malformed BC if the cert is included as an intermediate), BUT:
- The path builder still selects intermediate candidates whose BC is malformed → returned chain hits validate_path, which then runs signature verification and other checks before reaching the BC validation, wasting work.
- More importantly: a cert with malformed BC that the builder treats as \"not-CA\" is **rejected as a candidate intermediate**. So the builder may return Err(NoPathFound) when a topologically valid path exists through the malformed-BC cert. That cert was probably the right candidate; rejecting it silently produces a misleading error (NoPathFound vs the truthful \"there is a path but one of the intermediates is malformed\").

## Fix
Two reasonable options:
1. Propagate the parse error to the caller as a new \`Error::MalformedIntermediate\` variant.
2. Treat unparseable BC as a hard no, but log it via a tracing/diagnostic hook (currently no diagnostic surface in this crate).

Option 1 is more honest. Option 2 needs design.

## Scope reference
\`pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:154-166\`.
title: P2: pkix-path-builder cert_is_ca silently treats malformed BasicConstraints as not-CA
